Notes: Composite suite spanning many underlying scenario datasets; annotation/QC process varies per scenario and isn't centrally documented. Licensing is mixed/scenario-dependent across the underlying datasets, so reuse terms aren't uniformly clear.
Templates, ambiguous/disambiguated context design, and crowdworker validation are described in the paper. GitHub eval scripts are limited and the repo has seen little recent maintenance activity.

Dev-set items/labels are public, but the original evaluation relied partly on a held-out test set scored via leaderboard submission, limiting independent reproduction. Construct validity of the stereotype/ICAT score and annotation QC have been challenged by later external critiques (e.g., Blodgett et al. 2021) more than by the original documentation. Repo largely static since release.

Minimal-pair sentences, bias-type labels, and pseudo-log-likelihood scoring code are public. Crowdworker QC and data-quality issues were mainly surfaced by later external critiques (Blodgett et al. 2021) rather than original documentation; repo has occasional corrective updates but isn't actively maintained.

'Labels' are Perspective API toxicity scores rather than independent human annotations, so the annotation process is API documentation, not a human coding protocol. Coverage of demographic/domain categories beyond toxicity buckets is limited. Dataset is static on HF with no active versioning.

Functional test-case design, gold labels, and native-speaker validation process are clearly documented in the paper. Public evaluation tooling is thinner than the dataset itself; repo and license terms have not been actively updated since release.

Adversarial generation plus human-annotation (ALICE) process is described but is complex and only partially reproducible without the classifier itself. Independent later audits found label-quality issues not fully disclosed in the original docs. Code is MIT-licensed and public.

Most fully documented benchmark in this sample: public questions and reference answers, multiple explicit scoring protocols (MC1/MC2, GPT-judge), documented category coverage, and an actively used/maintained repo and HF dataset under a permissive license.

Behavior set and automated classifier-based grading pipeline are public and well documented. There are no fixed gold labels in the traditional sense since grading is classifier-based; behavior curation/QC process is less detailed than the eval framework. Some harmful-behavior artifacts have gated/restricted access for safety reasons, complicating full reuse.

Behavior dataset and live leaderboard pipeline are public with a clearly documented scoring methodology, but 'labels' rely on classifier judges rather than fixed gold annotations, and the human annotation/QC process for behavior curation is thin. Licensing is mixed (permissive code license, more restricted-use dataset terms).

Supplemental reliability benchmark. Please score using public documentation/artifacts only. — Open-ended generation prompts are public, but there are no fixed gold labels — bias is scored via external classifiers (sentiment/regard/toxicity), so 'labels' are only partially applicable. Domain/subgroup taxonomy (gender, race, religion, profession, political ideology) is clearly documented. Repo has seen little active maintenance since release.

Safety-sensitive. Do not inspect/copy raw harmful examples; use metadata/documentation only. — Behavior/target-string list is public and attack code (GCG) is public and widely used, but there is no formal harm taxonomy, no described curation/annotation process, and the original success-scoring approach (keyword/refusal matching) was later shown to be unreliable by follow-up work. License/reuse terms for the dataset itself are not clearly stated separately from the code license.

Safety/alignment benchmark. Use public documentation and metadata only. — Strong documentation overall: 14 harm categories are explicitly defined and covered, with a described crowd-annotation process (multiple annotators, QC) and a maintained PKU-Alignment HF/GitHub presence across dataset versions. Scoring for benchmark comparison (aggregating category-level safety labels into a single pass/fail or preference metric) is less standardized/explicit than e.g. TruthfulQA's MC1/MC2, so scored as partial.

Notes: Older benchmark; pay special attention to license, versioning, and evaluation-code clarity. — Coreference items and pro-/anti-stereotypical gold labels are public via the official site, and the accuracy-based scoring metric is clearly described in the original paper. The dataset is template/occupation-statistic generated rather than human-annotated, so annotation/QC process detail is thin. Coverage is narrow (binary gender, occupation-based bias only) and undocumented beyond that scope. The repo/site appear static since ~2018 with no ongoing versioning, and license terms are not prominently stated.
